codeReview.summary: The feature implementation is complete and correct, but was produced by a DIFFERENT commit (7ab6653) than the one referenced in the completing session's handoff (ee0aac7). Commit 7ab6653 adds 737 lines across reflection_agent.py and test_reflection.py, implementing correction detection (10 regex patterns + 5 false-positive filters), gap detection (8 AI uncertainty + 3 needs-info patterns), learning log integration, and daily reflection cycle integration. The code is well-structured with clear separation of concerns. Test coverage is comprehensive with 28 tests (11 correction, 11 gap, 2+2 integration, 2 daily cycle). The completing session (3ee87206) committed ee0aac7 which is entirely for the memory-context-assembly feature (test_context_assembly.py with 825 lines of context assembly pipeline tests) — NOT the memory-reflection-upgrade feature. Despite this session attribution error, the actual feature requirements are fully met in the codebase.

issues.description: Correction pattern `r"\bi\s+said\b.*\bnot\b"` is overly broad. The `.*` matches anything between 'I said' and 'not', so messages like 'I said yes, but it's not a problem' would be flagged as corrections. Consider tightening to require proximity or specific correction indicators after 'not'.

False-positive pattern `r"^\s*(?:why|how|when|what|where|is|are|can|could|should)\b"` filters ANY message starting with a question word. This is very broad — a message like 'Why did you get that wrong?' would be filtered even though it contains a legitimate correction. Consider narrowing this to only filter question-only messages.

In detect_gaps(), a single assistant message can produce TWO gap entries — one from _AI_UNCERTAINTY_PATTERNS and one from _AI_NEEDS_INFO_PATTERNS. Both loops iterate independently on the same message. Consider adding a flag to skip the second loop if the first already matched.

No deduplication of corrections or gaps before storing. If the same conversation thread is analyzed multiple times (e.g., across daily reflection runs), identical LEARNINGS/ERRORS entries will be created. Consider adding a dedup check against recently-stored entries.

test_no_false_positive_on_user_question has a weak assertion. It checks gaps but uses a vague condition that always passes ('assert ... or True'). The test should firmly assert that user-side 'I don't know' messages do NOT produce AI uncertainty gap entries.

summary: PASS with caveats. The memory-reflection-upgrade feature IS fully implemented in the codebase (commit 7ab6653): ReflectionAgent has correction detection (10 patterns + false-positive filtering), gap detection (AI uncertainty + missing context), learning log integration (corrections → LEARNINGS, gaps → ERRORS), daily reflection cycle integration, and 28 comprehensive tests. All expectedBehavior criteria are met. However, the completing worker session (3ee87206, commit ee0aac7) actually implemented tests for the memory-context-assembly feature instead — the handoff, commit, and transcript all describe context assembly work. The actual reflection upgrade was delivered by a different commit/session. Five non-blocking code quality issues noted: overly broad regex pattern, aggressive false-positive filtering, potential duplicate gap entries, no dedup across runs, and one weak test assertion.
